$comment: VAPP-289 (round 9 contract §14): upgrade09, the pure A2UI v0.9 → 1.0 converter. ONE fixture for the TS reference (src/upgrade09.ts) and the Rust core (eui-core upgrade09.rs); Swift and Kotlin replay two smoke cases through the FFI upgrade09Json. Inputs hand-written; `expected` recorded from the TS reference and reviewed against §14.3. Kinds: `message` = upgradeMessage09(input, emptyUpgrade09State()) → `expected` = its one message, `expectedState` = the state after; `stream` = `inputs` threaded through upgradeMessage09 from the empty state in order → `expected` = the concatenated messages, `expectedState` = the final state; `client` = upgradeClientMessage09(input); `card` = upgradeCard09(input); `package` = upgradePackageBody09(input) (a package object, no signature handling), or with `verify: true` upgradePackage09(input) with the default verifier (verifyPackageFile, Ed25519) → `expected` = {package, status, author?}. The signed files are signed with the RFC 8032 §7.1 TEST 1 keypair (fixtures/host-package.json `key`, name "Test Author"): public, NEVER a real author's; the invalid one is that file with `name` changed after signing. Messages, cards and packages compare as JSON with key order (§14.2: renamed keys in place, added keys at the end of their object, `version` first); `expectedState` compares as a map (key order free). State = {surfaces: {<surfaceId>: {<old id>: <new id>}}, catalogs: {<surfaceId>: <the createSurface catalogId, after the basic rewrite>}}; kept ids map to themselves.
